answer: Because the summit solution is checked at the shale gate and logged, the basalt audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 18 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
